                             PERSONAL INFORMATION:
                                                       Direct Testimony of TK Morris
                                                              PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                       Page 4 of 18
  1   Q. Please state your name and address.

 2   A. My name is TK Morris. My address is 272 County Rd 304 Seminole, Tx 79360

 3   Q. Are you an intervenor in this proceeding? If so, please explain how.

 4   A. Yes, I am participating as part of a group that has intervened in this proceeding on

 5   behalf of its members, the V8 Landowners Coalition, in PUC Docket Number 59475, link

 6   V8, I own Tract #4251:


 7   Q. Please state your familiarity with the property.


 8   A. Property has been in the family for 50, I have owned it for the past 4 yrs. Main use of

 9   the is agricultural, so someone is present everyday to keep an eye on livestock & crops.

10   Q. Are you testifying on your own or on behalf of another entity?


11      A. On my own behalf.

12   Q. What is the purpose of your testimony?


13      A. To block the V8 section of the 765 KV Transmission line.


14   Q. What is your overall concern with the proposed routing across/adjacent to

15   your property?

16      A. The devastating effect it will have on the land's production & Livestock's health.


17   Q. Have you ever testified at the Public Utility Commission of Texas before?

18   A. No

19                        PROPERTY DESCRIPTION AND LOCATION:

                                                                     Direct Testimony of TK Morris
                                                                            PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                   SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                     Page 5 of 18
  1   Q. Please describe your property.


 2      A. 350 acres of farmland, improved grassland & native pastureland.


 3   Q. Do you have pictures that support your description of your property?


 4      A. Yes

 5      B. Q. Where is your property located relative to the proposed routes?


 6   A. My property is parcel #4251, which is traversed by the V8 segment of the proposal.


 7   Q. Which routes affect your property?


 8   A. My property is affected by routes 74, 84, 93, 100, 391, 392, 402, 410, 416, 430, 442,

 9   453, 462, 589, 592, 1031, 1041, and 1055.


10   Q. What routes do you oppose or support?


11   A. I oppose routes 74, 84, 93, 100, 391, 392, 402, 410, 416, 430, 442, 453, 462, 589,

12   592, 1031, 1041, and 1055.


13                                 LAND USE AND HISTORY

14   Q. Please describe the history of your property and your association with it.


15      A. This has been farmland for many decades, used as Ranchland for livestock, I

16         have been on this property for 41 yrs.

17   How is the property currently used?




                                                                    Direct Testimony of TK Morris
                                                                           PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                  SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                    Page 6 of 18
  1   A. The property is used for farming crops to raising livestock, movement is always going

2    on at the farm, rotating livestock from one pasture to a different field. Moving

3    tractors/equipment from one field to another.

 4   Q. How would the proposed transmission line affect your use of the property?


 5   A. This transmission line would divide the property up into a north half & a south half.

6    Disrupting the flow of cattle from fields/pastures to pens, for shipping/receiving or

7    vaccination. Leveling water sources for the whole property, not just a part of the

 8   property.

 9                          COMMUNITY VALUES AND AESTHETICS

10   Q. How does your property contribute to community values?


11   A. This property contributes crop seed, hay & beef back to the community.


12   Q. How important are views and visual character to your property?


13   A. The views and visual character of my property are very important not just to me, but

14   as part of the rural character of this area. Properties like mine contribute to the overall

15   landscape and quality of life in this community. The ability to sit outside and enjoy the

16   natural setting is a core part of why people choose to live here, and the proposed
17   transmission line would significantly degrade that character.

18   Q. Are there areas that are routinely photographed, marketed, or publicly visible?


19   A. Several different fields I take pictures of to market crop/livestock production.

20   Q. How would the transmission line affect the aforementioned values?
                                                                       Direct Testimony of TK Morris
                                                                              PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                       Page 7 of 18
  1   A. It would cut down on the production of the ranch/farm business.


2    These impacts are directly relevant to the Commission's obligation to consider

3    community values and aesthetic impacts under §PURA 37.055(c)

 4                        HISTORICAL AND CULTURAL RESOURCES

 5   Q. Are there any cemeteries, burial sites, or family graveyards on your property?


6    A. No

 7   Q. Are there any archaeological sites or artifacts?


 8   A. Native American artifacts.


 9   Q. Are there any historic structures or historically significant features?


10   A. Native American artifacts.


11   Q. Have these resources been documented or surveyed?


12   A.

13   Q. Even if not formally documented, can you describe their history or

14   significance?

15   A. Partofthe Onion Creeklndianfight.

16   Q. Do you have any photographs, records, or other materials that show or

17   demonstrate any archaeological sites, artifacts, historic structures, or

18   historically significant features on your property?

19   A.
                                                                   Direct Testimony of TK Morris
                                                                          PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                 SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                   Page 8 of 18
  1   Q. How would the proposed routes affecting your property impact these

 2   resources?

 3   A.

 4                                ENVIRONMENTAL INTEGRITY

 5   Q. Are there environmentally sensitive areas on your property?


6    A. The property has many sensitive wildlife trails & habitat areas. The flow of migratory

7    birds through the seasonal onion creek flow.

 8   Q. Are there soils, slopes, or terrain features that present environmental risk?


9    A. I would be worried about crossing onion creek, about different erosion patterns &

10   wash outs.

11   Q. Do weather patterns, including wind and storm events, affect environmental

12   conditions on your property?

13   A. High winds contribute to tree loss, erosion, and disturbance of natural areas,

14   particularly following storms. Flooding rain contributes to erosion & disturbance of

15   natural areas. These conditions increase the sensitivity of the land to additional

16   disturbance such as clearing and construction.

17   Q. How would the project impact environmental conditions on your property?


18   A. Yes, would impact the natural water flow, downhills & the creek bed.


19

                                                                      Direct Testimony of TK Morris
                                                                             PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                    SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                      Page 9 of 18
  1                           WATER RESOURCES AND FLOODING

 2   Q. Have you observed flooding on your property?


3    A. Yes, flooded twice in the month of July in 2025. Washed miles of fenceline, eroded

 4   topsoil away. 2021 it rained 7" in 3 hrs, so it does happen seldomly often.

 5   Q. Are there floodplains, drainage features, or mapped BFEs on your property?


6    A. Onion creek is mapped, but does not show the flood plain through the creek bottom.

 7   Q. Are there creeks, springs, wetlands, or seeps present?


 8   A. Onion Creek

 9   Q. How do you think construction for this type of project could impact drainage

10   or flooding?

11   A. Change natural flow of drainage water at or near the tower sites & easement.

12                          WATER SUPPLY AND GROUNDWATER

13   Q. Do you rely on groundwater wells?


14   A. Yes the whole place relies on water wells.


15   Q. Are you located within a groundwater conservation district?


16   A. Yes, Hickory Underground Water Conservation District.

17   Q. What risks do you anticipate this project could pose to your water supply?




                                                                     Direct Testimony of TK Morris
                                                                            PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                   SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                    Page 10 of 18
  1   A. Condemn the main water well & source. Relocation of water wells in this country is

2    not a for sure deal, even if there is a near by water well.

 3                                    AGRICULTURAL OPERATIONS

 4   Q. What agricultural or land management activities occur on your property?


 5   A. Plowing, Spraying, Mowing, Planting, Baling & Combining. We build dams & tanks to

6    conserve water & slow down erosion.

 7   Q. Are there seasonal operations, such as calving, harvesting, and/or hunting?


 8   A. Calving, Lambing are happing every month, Harvesting is spring & fall business.

9    Hunting is fall to the spring.


10   Q. How would construction interfere with these operations?


11   A. Calving or Lambing would be disturbed from bring in livestock to the pens to be

12   worked or medically checked out. All harvesting would be disturbed by logistically

13   getting to grain storage to the field. Hunting would be disrupted by wildlife not being

14   attracted to the magnetic field created by the transmission lines.

15                    ENGINEERING, ACCESS, AND CONSTRUCTABILITY

16   Q. Are there limitations to accessing your property?


17   A. In high flooding there is impacted access to the property.


18   Q. Are there terrain or soil constraints?




                                                                       Direct Testimony of TK Morris
                                                                              PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                      Pag e 11 of 18
  1   A. Ground could stay wet if the drainage in near the creek is changed to where it could

2    not drain, to become a marsh.

 3   Q. Are there conflicts with existing infrastructure?


 4   A. Many underground water pipe lines throughout the proptery, overhead utility lines to

 5   structures & wells.

 6   Q. How do you think the soil constraints and existing infrastructure could affect

 7   the construction, maintenance, or safety of these lines?

 8   A. If ground stays wet, it can shift and move the towers to cause significant damage.


 9   Q. Have you experienced significant wind or storm events on your property?


10   A. Yes, downed trees with straight-line winds, move objects from Mini tornadoes, toe

11   barns, barn roofs & a porch off a house.

12   Q. Can you please describe the impacts that these events have had on your

13   property?

14   A. es, downed trees with straight-line winds, move objects from Mini tornadoes, toe

15   barns, barn roofs & a porch off a house. No access to the house.

16   Q. Based on your experience with wind and storms, do you have concerns about

17   conductor movement, line sag, or structural stress?

18   A. Wind or/and tornadoes could bring down these structures & cause severe damage.




                                                                    Direct Testimony of TK Morris
                                                                           PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                  SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                   Page 12 of 18
  1   Q. How do you believe the conditions mentioned in this section could affect

 2   construction, maintenance, or safety related to the proposed transmission lines?

3    A. I am concerned about the interaction between high winds, vegetation, and large

 4   structures or lines near areas where people live and spend time during my

 5   farm/ranching operation.

 6                  PRUDENT AVOI DANCE AND HABITABLE STRUCTURES

 7   Q: Please describe all habitable structures on your property.


 8   A. Main dwelling/home, may equipment and livestock barns.


 9   Q: Are there any habitable structures within 500 feet of the proposed centerline?


10   A. norther barn is within 500' of the centerline.


11   Q: Beyond the home itself, are there outdoor living areas, such as patios, pools,

12   and/or porches within 500 feet of the propose centerline?

13   A. No.

14   Q. How close are the proposed routes to these structures?


15   A.

16   Q. How frequently are the aforementioned structures and areas occupied?


17   A.

18   Q. What areas of your property are most actively used?



                                                                   Direct Testimony of TK Morris
                                                                          PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                 SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                  Page 13 of 18
  1   A. 3 out of the 4 fields the transmission line crosses are heavy used/active areas for the

2    livestock operation.

 3   Q. Does the current route placement require you to move any existing structures

 4   or hinder your ability to build planned structures?

 5   A.

 6   Q. How does the proposed routing fail to avoid higher-impact areas?


7    A. Goes through 3 main pastures on the property to run livestock to grazing areas to

 8   pens and barns.

 9   Q. Do you believe the proposed routing reflects prudent avoidance?


10   A. No, I don't believe the routing reflects avoidance of my barn structures, water wells &

11   watering facilities. It runs through the heaviest areas of running livestock to doctoring
12   sick & bringing in other to pens for shipping.

13                          CUMULATIVE IMPACTS AND CONSTRAINTS

14   Q. Are there any other existing or proposed infrastructure projects affecting your

15   property?

16   A. No

17   Q. Were these projects planned or disclosed to you at the same time?


18   A.

19   Q. How does the compressed timeline affect your ability to respond or adapt?

                                                                       Direct Testimony of TK Morris
                                                                              PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                      Page 14 of 18
  1   A.

 2   Q. How would the proposed transmission line interact with these other projects

 3   on your property?

 4   A.

 5   Q. What challenges would result from multiple infrastructure projects affecting

 6   your property at the same time?

7    A.

 8   Q. Do you believe it is reasonable or feasible to accommodate multiple large

 9   infrastructure projects on your property within the current timeframe?

10   A. No, this property is not large enough to support large infrastructure projects & still run

11   a family business.

12   Q. How do these combined constraints affect your ability to use, access, or

13   manage your property?

14   A. Harder to access anther section of the property one side to another and manage

15   livestock back and forth.

16   Q. How many acres of "open land" area would be bisected by this new 200' right-

17   of-way?

18   A. 350 acres

19   Q. Does the route create a "new" corridor where none currently exist?


                                                                       Direct Testimony of TK Morris
                                                                              PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                      Page 15 of 18
  1   A. Yes.

 2                                    FINANCIAL IMPACTS

 3   Q. What features of your property contribute to its value?


 4   A. Water flow, water well, rich nutrient soil for farm and harvest many different crops &

 5   grasses.

 6   Q. How would those features be affected by the proposed line?


7    A. It would cut down on the valve & volume of production.


 8   Q. Do you have solar panels or other on-site energy systems on your property?


9    A. No

10   Q. How are these systems used?


11   A.

12   Q. How could the proposed transmission line affect these systems?


13   A.

14   Q. What investment have you made in these systems, and how important are

15   they to your property?

16   A.

17   Q. What financial risks do you believe this project presents?




                                                                     Direct Testimony of TK Morris
                                                                            PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                   SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                    Page 16 of 18
  1   A. I have financial risk of not making a profitable business from this Family Orientated

2    Business.

 3   Q. How do you believe your property value will be affected?


 4   A. Yes, it will devastate it.


 5                             LOCAL ELECTRIC SERVICE AND NEED

 6   Q. Do you believe this project will improve electric service in your area?


7    A. No, no power for this county, just bringing it further east.


 8   Q. Do you believe it will reduce your electricity cost?


9    A. No.

10                                   SUPPORTING EVIDENCE

11   Q. Do you have any documents supporting your testimony?

12   A. Pictures of the property.


13   Q. Are these materials true and correct representations?

14   A. Yes.

15   Q. Do they fairly and accurately depict the conditions described?


16   A. Yes.

17                                    SUMMARY OF IMPACTS



                                                                         Direct Testimony of TK Morris
                                                                                PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                       SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                        Page 17 of 18
  1   Q. Can you summarize the primary impacts this project would have on your

 2   property?

3    A. Lower land production, cost more time to operate, devalue the water source if not

 4   destroy them. Deny access to minerals below ground level. Cutoff aerial application to

 5   any farm land under the towers.

 6   Q. What would be the single most significant impact of this project on your

 7   property?

 8   A. Devalue the business. Cut off water supply to the whole property, by condemning the

9    main water well.

10                        CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS

11   Q. Based on your testimony, do any of the routes involving your property best

12   meet the statutory criteria of considering community values, environmental

13   integrity, and/or land use compatibility?

14   A. No.

15   Q. What action would you like the Commission to take?

16   A. I/We want the Commission to abandon routes 74, 84, 93, 100, 391, 392, 402, 410,

17   416, 430, 442, 453, 462, 589, 592, 1031, 1041, and 1055 containing link V8 and utilize

18   a route with fewer constraints.

19   Q. Does this conclude your testimony?


20   A. Yes.
